newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - down about 3/8 point on day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - down about 3/8 point on day.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices lost about 3/8 point Friday but recovered slightly from the day's lows, traders said.
One analyst said actively traded dollar bonds were off even more, down about 1/2 point, but that was mostly because of low activity levels.
"I think if there had been active trading, they probably would have been only off 3/8," the analyst said.

Market participants continued to cite extremely low new issue supply as worrisome, with just $1.2 billion of new issues on the calendar for next week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
"Its like the year hasn't even started yet," said Richard Visconti, head of muni trading at WR Lazard & Co. "It's scary."
Next week's competitive sales total $491 million in 51 issues, with the largest just $50 million from the West Virginia Housing Development Fund issue on Tuesday.
Negotiated sales total $696 million in 21 offerings. The largest is a $134 million Suffolk County Industrial Development Authority, N.Y., deal through Smith Barney Inc.
While munis lost about 3/8, the government long bond dropped 13/32 to 95-2/32, showing a 6.89 percent yield heading into the New York close.
Treasuries also pared some losses late in the day, but the tone continues to be bearish.
In the muni secondary, bids on Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were up four basis points from Thursday, at 5.89 percent net.
Delaware River Port Authority FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 were up five basis points to 5.75 percent net.
Futures also ended lower, with the March municipal contract down 15/32 on the day to 114-1/32. March T-bonds lost 19/32 to 110-8/32. The MOB spread widened to 121 from 117 at the close on Thursday.
